topic.name: Determining Indexes of Terms in Geometric Sequences

question.text:
What is the index of the term $96$ for the geometric sequence below?

\[ a_{n+1} = 4 a_n, \quad a_1 = 6,\quad n\geq 1 \]
question.explanation:
This geometric sequence is given as a recurrence relation, i.e.,

\[ a_{n+1} = r \cdot a_n. \]

Therefore, \[ a_1 = 6, \quad r=4. \]

We're interested in finding $n$ such that $a_n =96.$ Using the formula for the $n$th term, we get:

\begin{align} a_n & = a_1 \cdot r^{n-1} \\[5pt] 96 & = 6 \cdot 4^{n-1}\\[5pt] \dfrac{96}{6} & = 4^{n-1}\\[5pt] 16 & = 4^{n-1}\\[5pt] 4^{2} &= 4^{n-1} \end{align}

Equating the exponents gives: \[ 2 = n - 1\quad \Longrightarrow \quad n = 3 \]

Therefore, $96$ is the $3$rd term of the sequence.

example.title: Finding the Index of a Term Given the Recursive Formula

question.text: What is the index of the term $640$ for the geometric sequence below? \[ f(n+1) = 4f(n), \quad f(1) = 10, \quad n\geq 1 \]
question.explanation:
This geometric sequence is given as a recurrence relation, i.e.,

\[ f(n+1) = r \cdot f(n). \]

Therefore: \[ f(1) = 10, \quad r=4. \]

We're interested in finding $n$ such that $f(n) = 640.$ Using the formula for the $n$th term, we get:

\begin{align*} f(n) &= f(1)\cdot r^{n-1}\\[5pt] 640 & = 10 \cdot 4^{n-1}\\[5pt] \dfrac{640}{10} & = 4^{n-1}\\[5pt] 64 & = 4^{n-1}\\[5pt] 4^{3} &= 4^{n-1} \end{align*}

Equating the exponents gives: \[ 3 = n - 1 \quad \Longrightarrow \quad n = 4 \]

Therefore, $640$ is the $4$th term of the sequence.

example.title: Finding the Index of a Term Given the Recursive Formula

question.text: Given that a geometric sequence has the $4$th term $a_4 = 250$ and the common ratio $r = 5$, what is the index of the term $1\,250?$
question.explanation:
Since we are given that $a_4 = 250$, we can use the formula for the $n$th term to solve for $a_1$, as follows:

\begin{align*} a_4&=a_1 \cdot r^{4-1}\\[5pt] 250 & = a_1 \cdot 5 ^ {4 - 1}\\[5pt] 250 & = a_1 \cdot 5^{3}\\[5pt] \dfrac{250}{125} & = a_1\\[5pt] a_1 & = 2 \end{align*}

Therefore, the formula for the $n$th term is

\begin{align*} a_n = 2 \cdot 5^{n-1}. \end{align*}

Now, we solve for the value of $n$ that gives $a_n=1\,250,$ as follows:

\begin{align*} 1\,250 & = 2 \cdot 5^ {n - 1}\\[5pt] \dfrac{1\,250}2 & = 5 ^ {n - 1}\\[5pt] 625 & = 5 ^ {n - 1}\\[5pt] 5^4 & = 5 ^{n -1} \end{align*}

Equating the exponents gives: \[ 4 = n - 1\quad \Longrightarrow \quad n = 5 \]
